text_blocks.snippet: Approximately 1 in 5 children and adolescents (ages 3-17) in the U.S. have been diagnosed with a mental, emotional, or behavioral health condition. A significant portion of youth experience persistent sadness or hopelessness, serious suicidal thoughts, and even suicide attempts. Rates of youth mental health conditions, particularly anxiety and depression, have been increasing in recent years.
snippet_highlighted_words: Approximately 1 in 5 children and adolescents (ages 3-17) in the U.S. have been diagnosed with a mental, emotional, or behavioral health condition

list.snippet: 1 in 5 (21%): children ages 3-17 have been diagnosed with a mental, emotional, or behavioral health condition.
50%: of lifetime mental illnesses begin by age 14.
49.5%: of adolescents have experienced a mental health disorder at some point in their lives, according to the National Institute of Mental Health.
1 in 6: youth aged 6-17 experience a mental health disorder each year.

list.title: Anxiety:
list.snippet: Anxiety disorders are common among adolescents, with higher prevalence rates among older adolescents than younger ones.

list.title: Depression:
list.snippet: Depression is also prevalent among adolescents, with higher rates among older adolescents.

list.title: Suicidal Thoughts and Behaviors:
list.snippet: A concerning number of youth report experiencing suicidal ideation (seriously considering suicide) and attempting suicide.

list.title: Major Depressive Episodes:
list.snippet: Approximately 1 in 5 youth (ages 12-17) experience a major depressive episode in the past year.

list.title: Increasing Rates:
list.snippet: There is evidence that mental health conditions, particularly anxiety and depression, are becoming more prevalent among youth.

list.title: Pandemic Impact:
list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has exacerbated existing mental health challenges and contributed to increased rates of sadness, hopelessness, and difficulty with schoolwork among youth.

list.title: Social Media and Technology:
list.snippet: Increased time spent on social media and online activities may be contributing factors to mental health challenges, particularly for girls.

list.title: Systemic Factors:
list.snippet: Issues like racism, violence, and climate change can also negatively impact youth mental health, according to experts.

list.title: LGBTQ+ Youth:
list.snippet: LGBTQ+ youth are disproportionately affected, with higher rates of suicidal ideation and attempts.

list.title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities:
list.snippet: Some racial and ethnic groups, such as Native American youth, experience higher rates of suicide compared to the national average.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: While many youth experience mental health challenges, a significant portion do not receive the necessary treatment.

list.title: Importance of Early Intervention:
list.snippet: Early intervention and treatment can greatly improve outcomes for young people with mental health disorders.

list.title: Help-Seeking Behaviors:
list.snippet: Girls are more likely to seek mental health therapy or counseling compared to boys.
